generation: Use case: stylized-concept. Production 2D side-scrolling palace background ARCHITECTURE LAYER with real transparent alpha window openings. Reference image is the existing game gallery: match its nearly black architectural masses, desaturated antique brass lines, very dark oxblood carpet, matte restrained texture, flat silhouette illustration exactly. Create ONE CONTINUOUS panorama of the FULL glass gallery AND its right-end 90-degree turn into a short receding passage. Wide 3:1 canvas, preferably 3072x1024. Left 75 percent: long side-view gallery with 8 tall arched glass window openings, sparse thin piers, high dark ceiling, two sparse chandeliers. Right 25 percent: the SAME gallery floor bends smoothly AWAY from viewer into the distance around the end corner, with 3 diminishing arches, reaching a small left-turn doorway at the far end. This is real architectural continuity: shared uninterrupted floor, matching skirting lines, cornices and ceiling, same column thickness, no vertical pasted-image boundary, no separate inset illustration or picture frame. The near walking line runs horizontally at 90 percent image height and bends back only in the rightmost quarter, where the far threshold is around 65 percent image height. End passage is HUMAN-SCALE, same ceiling as gallery, not a giant cathedral or a glowing portal. Match the dim near-black and weathered muted brass palette of the reference THROUGHOUT, including the turning passage; never vivid red/purple or shiny yellow gold. Floor same dark red carpet throughout, dark stone edges. Only window interiors are fully transparent holes to show separate courtyard layers. Wall, ceiling and continuous floor opaque. No outside view painted in the window openings: no trees, buildings, sky, clouds, scenery. No props, furniture, characters, text, diagram labels or arrows. Do not leave a black opaque fill or checkerboard pattern in the glass: alpha transparent. Keep pillars thin, floor clean, no overdecorating. Full artwork edge to edge.

Use case: stylized-concept. An isolated wide horizontal exterior architectural layer for a 2D palace courtyard parallax scene. Reference gives the EXACT silhouette/brass style: nearly-black charcoal and muted slate with restrained faded brass edges. Subject is the CLOSED CORRIDOR WING on the OPPOSITE SIDE of a small courtyard, a NEARBY SINGLE-STORY rectangular palace corridor building, very long and low, seen straight-on from the glass gallery across the courtyard. It is the return leg of a U-shaped palace route. Solid continuous walls with a simple cornice, repeating shallow arched wall panels, a few narrow dark shuttered openings and one small arched end entrance, restrained flat roofline. Consistent palace style. Clear sharp contours, readable solid architecture, not blurred atmospheric scenery, no faraway city or village or monumental distant castle. Very wide 3:1 transparent canvas, building occupying almost all width with small transparent margins. Around and above the isolated wing fully transparent. No ground foreground, no trees/plants, no sky, no mountains, no people, no text, no perspective street. Separate tree layers will stand in front of this. No bright purple, saturated gold, reflections or 3D lighting. Dark matte black/blue-gray silhouette with subtle old brass trims, sparse detail; enough tonal separation from near-black foreground windowframes to read at night.
